Fiddler on the Roof. The nineteen sixty-four musical by Jerry Bock, music, and Sheldon Harnick, lyrics, set in the Jewish village of Anatevka in tsarist Russia. Centered on the patriarch Tevye and his five daughters, it explores tradition, love, social change, and displacement, ultimately capturing the dissolution of a way of life as pogroms and migration uproot the community.

This was their most enduring collaboration, earning nine Tony Awards in nineteen sixty-five. The opening number "Tradition" immediately establishes both the rigidity and the vulnerability of Jewish communal life in the Pale of Settlement. Famous songs include "If I Were a Rich Man," often performed as a comic patter song, "Matchmaker, Matchmaker," "Sunrise, Sunset," "To Life," and "Anatevka."

Tevye, the protagonist, engages in comic and philosophical dialogue with God, and his debates with each daughter about marriage choices drive the plot's emotional arc. The musical is set against the historical backdrop of Russian pogroms from nineteen three to nineteen oh-six. It uses folk idiom and klezmer-influenced orchestration to ground the story in Jewish cultural authenticity.

The show ran on Broadway for thirty-two hundred forty-two performances from nineteen sixty-four to nineteen seventy-two, the longest-running Broadway show at the time, and has become a canonical staple. The nineteen seventy-one film, directed by Norman Jewison, won three Academy Awards and introduced the musical to global audiences. Zero Mostel originated the role of Tevye.
